stem: Which of the following best describes a computer network?
options: an interconnection of two or more computing devices
a single computer running several programs at once
a group of programs stored together on one hard disk
a set of cables used to supply power to computers
explanation: Correct option: (A). A computer network is an interconnection among two or more computers or computing devices that lets them share data and resources. A single computer running many programs is multitasking, not networking; programs stored on one disk are just files; and power cables carry electricity, not data between devices.

stem:
Arrange the following milestones of networking in chronological order:
(i) TCP/IP introduced as the standard protocol on ARPANET
(ii) Berners-Lee at CERN develops HTML and URL, giving birth to the WWW
(iii) ARPANET becomes functional by connecting UCLA and SRI
(iv) The first version of the Wi-Fi (802.11) standard is introduced
explanation: Correct option: (D). ARPANET connected UCLA and SRI in 1969, TCP/IP became ARPANET's standard protocol in 1983, the WWW was born in 1990 and the first Wi-Fi (802.11) standard came in 1997. Placing TCP/IP before ARPANET itself is impossible because TCP/IP was introduced on ARPANET; putting the WWW before TCP/IP or Wi-Fi before the WWW reverses the actual dates.

stem: At the sender's end, a modem acts as a:
options: demodulator, converting digital data into analog signals
modulator, converting analog signals into digital data
modulator, converting digital data into analog signals
demodulator, converting analog signals into digital data
explanation: Correct option: (C). The sender's modem modulates: it converts the computer's digital data into analog signals that the medium can carry. stem: Which statement about an Ethernet card (NIC) is correct?
options: It has a MAC address that identifies the computer on the network.
It converts digital data into analog signals for telephone lines.

stem:
Assertion (A): When two computers communicate over a telephone line, a modem is required at both the sender's and the receiver's end.
Reason (R): Computers store and process data as digital bits, while the telephone line carries analog signals.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Both statements are true, and R explains A. Because computers work with digital bits but the line carries analog signals, the sender's modem must modulate (digital to analog) and the receiver's modem must demodulate (analog to digital); a modem at only one end would leave one computer unable to understand the signal.

stem: What is the main limitation of an Ethernet hub?
options: It cannot connect more than two devices at the same time.
It sends data only to the intended destination device.
It converts all the digital data into analog signals.
Data arriving from two devices together may collide.
explanation: Correct option: (D). A hub sends data arriving on any line out on all the other lines, so if data from two devices arrive at the same time they collide. A hub has many ports (for example, 8), sending only to the intended device is what a switch does, and converting digital to analog is the work of a modem.

stem: A packet arrives at a network switch. Which of the following describes what the switch does with it?
options: Sends it out on all its other ports so that every device receives a copy.
Finds its destination in a table and sends it to that device only.
Converts it into an analog signal and sends it out over a telephone line.
Regenerates its signal and forwards it unchanged on every connected cable.
explanation: Correct option: (B). A switch extracts the destination address from the packet, looks it up in a table and sends it only to the selected device; it also drops noisy or corrupted signals. Sending to every port is how a hub behaves, converting to analog is a modem's job, and regenerating the signal on all cables describes neither a switch nor its forwarding decision.

stem: Based on the case, which choice of devices best meets Ms. Rao's three requirements?
options: a hub in the lab and a repeater working as the gateway
a switch in the lab and a router working as the gateway
a switch in the lab and a modem working as the firewall
a hub in the lab and a switch working as the gateway
explanation: Correct option: (B). Requirement (i) needs a switch, which forwards each packet only to its destination PC instead of broadcasting like a hub. Requirements (ii) and (iii) need a gateway at the edge of the network; a router is generally configured to work as the gateway, and because the gateway sits at the network edge the firewall is usually integrated with it. A hub fails requirement (i), a repeater only regenerates signals, a modem only converts signals, and a switch connects devices within a LAN rather than acting as the gateway.

options: exactly two neighbouring devices in a ring
every other device in the whole network

stem: In an office network, when the cable of one computer is damaged only that computer is cut off, but when the central device fails the entire network stops working. The network uses:
explanation: Correct option: (C). In star topology a fault in one device or its cable does not affect the rest of the network, but failure of the central hub or switch brings down the whole network. stem:
Assertion (A): A bus topology is cheaper and easier to maintain than a mesh topology.
Reason (R): In a bus topology, the link is unidirectional, so data flows along the bus in one direction only.

stem: Which description of an IPv6 address is correct?
options: 32 bits, written as four decimal numbers separated by periods
48 bits, written as twelve hexadecimal digits in six pairs
64 bits, written as eight groups of decimal numbers with dots
128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal numbers

stem: A network card has the MAC address 3C:5A:B4:12:9F:07. Which part of it is the Organisational Unique Identifier (OUI)?
explanation: Correct option: (B). The first six hexadecimal digits (24 bits) of a MAC address are the manufacturer's ID, called the OUI, so here it is 3C:5A:B4. stem: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long and IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long. How many times larger is the number of possible IPv6 addresses than the number of possible IPv4 addresses?
explanation: Correct option: (C). Number of IPv6 addresses / number of IPv4 addresses = 2^128 / 2^32 = 2^(128-32) = 2^96. '4 times' divides the bit lengths (128/32) instead of the address counts; '96 times' subtracts the bit lengths but forgets they are powers of 2; '2^160 times' adds the exponents (128 + 32) instead of subtracting them when dividing.

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Internet from the World Wide Web?

The web is a type of LAN, while the Internet is the largest WAN in the world.
